what: A write-only lane pins the kernel's carry counts (`Carried`) as predictions it cannot run. I predicted `parse` changes on every text edit; it does not: `parse(file)`'s value (`syntax::image`) is the tree's shape and holds no text, so an edit that swaps a token for one of the same kind and length is cut at `parse`. The main agent's run caught it (changed 1, cut 2 where I wrote 2, 1).
cost: one compile-and-test round trip of the main agent
cause: what a step's value holds is said in a doc line of steps.rs (`the record shares it, it does not hold it`), not where a reader of the value would look first (the step's own doc or the value's type)
class: a prediction stated as a pinned number without evidence from a run (rule 61)
prevention: a write-only lane marks every pinned count it has not seen as a prediction in its report, and states for each step what its value holds and what it reads directly (the cutoff test's `carried` doc now does)
workaround: the test's doc says why parse is cut
fix: the corrected count and its reason in cutoffs.rs
